title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether Staff of Foreign Embassies in China May, in the Capacity of Diplomatic Representatives, Hire Chinese Lawyers for Their Nationals in Civil Litigation in China

articles.content_en:
Supreme People's Court
Reply on Whether Staff Members of Foreign Embassies in China May Engage Chinese Lawyers on Behalf of Their Nationals in Civil Actions in the Capacity of Diplomatic Agents
March 28, 1985 (1985) Min Ta Zi No. 5
Shanghai Higher People's Court:
We have received your request for instructions No. (85) Hu Gao Min Shang Zi No. 5 dated January 10, 1985. Regarding the question of whether a Counsellor of the Embassy of Switzerland in China may, in the capacity of a diplomatic agent, engage a Chinese lawyer on behalf of his national for representation in a civil action in China, upon study, we are of the opinion that, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations and the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations, to which China is a party, the engagement of a lawyer by the Embassy of Switzerland in China upon the mandate of its nationals Li Meiti and Li Aiwei constitutes an official function of the embassy. Therefore, it is permissible for the embassy to authorize its staff member to engage Chinese lawyers on behalf of Li Meiti and Li Aiwei in civil actions in China in the capacity of a diplomatic agent.
Reply hereby.
